migration.description: Version PostgreSQL analytics replica fact-date semantics, mark existing replica state as legacy, and require a separately authorized bounded rebuild before service eligibility.
migration.release_unit_description: PG18 analytics fact-date compatibility and replica bootstrap safety follow-up.

durable_state.description: PostgreSQL analytics_replica_state semantic-version marker, normalized analytics facts, parallel-work membership, applied-change journal, and replica checkpoints.
durable_state.storage_implementation: PostgreSQL cvm_analytics schema populated from the existing SQLite analytics source journal.

source_compatibility_range.from_program_versions: Supported 0.2.x schemas with no fact_date_semantics_version column or with legacy version 1 state.

ddl_structural_changes.description: The schema owner applies the reviewed additive fact_date_semantics_version column with default 1 for an existing replica table; fresh tables declare the current default 2. Application startup and maintenance commands never execute this DDL.

dml_changes.description: The dedicated maintenance role serializes explicit bootstrap, clears facts, applied changes, parallel-work keys, and checkpoints in one bounded target transaction sequence, rebuilds current-semantic facts, and publishes version 2 only after the baseline and source acknowledgement commit.

historical_data_backfill_or_transformati.description: No automatic historical fact backfill or query/rollup transformation runs. Existing facts are replaced only by an explicitly invoked bounded bootstrap after the schema-owner step; fact identity and journal event version 1 remain unchanged.

progress_signals: pg_catalog confirms the compatibility column before maintenance bootstrap begins.
Replica status exposes bootstrapping, caught_up, invalidated, blocked, and service_eligible state with the semantic version and checkpoints.
The explicit bootstrap lock and bounded batch limits remain observable in maintenance output and failure details.
pause_points: After schema-owner DDL and before maintenance grants or bootstrap.
After target cleanup/checkpoint reset and before each bounded snapshot batch.
After the bounded rebuild and before source acknowledgement publishes eligibility.

recovery.program_rollback_state_behavior: Earlier programs may ignore the additive column, but the current v2 bootstrap keeps the shared legacy-visible service_eligible flag false so those programs fail closed; no rollback removes the column or marks corrected facts service eligible under legacy semantics.
recovery.faulty_release_recovery: A newer compatible program re-enters the explicit owner-schema step if required, then reruns the serialized maintenance bootstrap forward. A failed bootstrap leaves the target unavailable or blocked and never silently enables reads; backup restore remains separate disaster recovery.

required_test_evidence: Deterministic unit contracts cover Shanghai date boundaries, version eligibility, CAS invalidation, target cleanup, advisory-lock SQL, and unchanged fact/journal identities.
The explicitly ignored PostgreSQL fixture test verifies owner/app/maintenance role separation, pg_catalog visibility, advisory-lock contention, and bounded target reset against a disposable database.
A stopped or failed bootstrap remains unavailable and can be repaired forward by a later explicit bootstrap without automatic historical backfill.
